LESSON: WORD CLASS: CONJUNCTIONS

Grade: Grade 5
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 10
Topic 10.3.1: Word Class: Conjunctions

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Word Class: Conjunctions. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Why do you join words and sentences?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. identify conjunctions: but, or, yet, because, since and also, in texts for effective communication
2. use conjunctions but, or, yet, because, since and also, correctly in communication

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE LEARNING: WORD CLASS: CONJUNCTIONS
This lesson teaches Word Class: Conjunctions for Grade 5 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

STUDY STEPS
1. identify conjunctions: but, or, yet, because, since and also, in texts for effective communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.
2. use conjunctions but, or, yet, because, since and also, correctly in communication
   Practise this until you can do it without help.

HOW TO SHOW UNDERSTANDING
Explain the idea in your own words, give one Kenyan example, then complete the practice tasks.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Describe Word Class: Conjunctions using something at your school.

Example 2: Give a home/community example from your county.

Example 3: Teach a younger child one idea from this lesson in simple words.

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Underline the key ideas about Word Class: Conjunctions above.
2. Explain Word Class: Conjunctions to a parent using one local example.
3. Write or draw three things that prove you understand Word Class: Conjunctions.

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. Write five sentences about Word Class: Conjunctions with school or home examples.
2. Answer: Why is Word Class: Conjunctions important for a Grade 5 learner?
3. Prepare a one-minute oral presentation for a parent or teacher.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Why do you join words and sentences?
2. How do you join words or sentences?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. identify conjunctions: but, or, yet, because, since and also, in texts for effective communication
2. use conjunctions but, or, yet, because, since and also, correctly in communication

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
